Moving the nightly report to the new queue

Plan v2 · written for review

The nightly report is built by a single script that reads every order from the database, formats it, and emails a summary at six in the morning. It works, but it takes forty minutes and fails quietly when the database is slow. This plan moves the work onto the job queue we already run for invoices.

What changes

Three things move. The script is split into small jobs, one per region. Each job writes its result to a table instead of building the email in memory. A last job collects the rows and sends the email once every region has reported.

  • Each region runs as its own job, so one slow region no longer holds up the rest.
  • Failed jobs retry three times and then raise an alert to the on-call channel.
  • The email is sent by one job that waits for all regions, with a ten minute limit.

The approach

We keep the same report layout and the same recipients. Only the plumbing changes. The old script stays in place for one week behind a switch, so we can fall back by changing a single setting.

StepOwnerWhen
Split the script into region jobsDanaWeek 1
Write results to the report tableDanaWeek 1
Add the collecting email jobMarcoWeek 2
Run both versions side by sideMarcoWeek 3

The rollout

In week three both versions send an email, and we compare the numbers by hand every morning. If the totals match for five days in a row, we turn the old script off. If they do not match, we stay on the old script and fix the difference first.

The switch back takes about a minute: set REPORT_MODE=legacy and the scheduler ignores the new jobs.

Open questions

Do we want the on-call alert for a single failed region, or only when two or more fail? A single failure is usually a slow database and clears on retry.
